data.narrative:
Irradiant Technologies is a Seed-stage robotics and manufacturing company founded by Daniel Oran and Amos Meeks that has raised $8.5M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a comp universe of 9 private companies and 1 public entity operating in the broader Robotics & Manufacturing sector.

Stage-progression methodology is the primary applicable valuation approach, using total capital raised as a proxy baseline. Applying a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical of Seed-to-next-stage progression yields an implied valuation of $21M. A peer-median approach could not be reliably applied due to insufficient narrow-set comparables; while 11 same-sector peers exist, clustering by stage and valuation tier produced fewer than three datapoints, making sector-wide median estimates unreliable.

The triangulation supports a valuation range of $18M to $24M, with a median point of $21M. This range reflects the 2.5x progression framework applied to the $8.5M raised base. Key uncertainties include the absence of tight-stage comparables in the robotics subsector, which limits cross-validation; the reliance on a single progression method rather than multiple independent approaches; and the early stage of the company, which typically carries higher valuation variance. The range should be treated as indicative pending additional operational milestones or expanded peer data.
